revision_relation: verified PR #9 head; tree equals the initial local unified-research checkout
board_assumptions: Board index 1 and the shipped INI fields are inputs for the five pinned releases.
OBS-001 samples a single running Koriki device. TF1/SD2 is reconciled to that boot; TF2 pad routing remains inferred.
Power, GPIO and DRAM responses in the trace are synthetic.
limitations: No physical ROM state, SRAM extent, reset values, analog training, rail voltages or DRAM part identification.
No continuous U-Boot startup or relocation, and kernel execution stops before the first instruction.
Proposed profile constraints do not certify any register value or ordering for physical use.
The reviewed unified-research revision is pinned. Local preliminary replay used an identical repository tree.

rom.input_state: ROM startup complete in the model
rom.observed_output: First sector, CMU gate seed, ARM stack and CPSR supplied
rom.independent_constraint: Establish load and entry rules before relying on ROM behavior.

sram.input_state: Dispatched SD route and accessible ROM service by hypothesis
sram.observed_output: Loader and INI installed; globals formed in SRAM
sram.independent_constraint: Prove writable/executable ownership and stack capacity before any stack use.

power.input_state: Board profile and live early-access clock/timer
power.observed_output: UART diagnostics, PMIC identity checks, power and wake fields
power.independent_constraint: Qualify rails and isolate board-specific pin, GPIO and PMIC policies.

selection.input_state: INI version plus PMIC/GPIO and configuration
selection.observed_output: Cold or resume state, or recovery terminal
selection.independent_constraint: Separate cold and retention paths and classify failures before DRAM use.

dram.input_state: Record, clock and power conditions, hardware responses
dram.observed_output: Controller/PHY setup, training, decoded size or typed failure
dram.independent_constraint: Require appropriate readiness and reject unsupported, failed or unproven memory.

handoff.input_state: Cold caller outcomes and selected record
handoff.observed_output: SRAM write-back and AFI; dispatch from actual caller result
handoff.independent_constraint: Treat AFI and the diagnostic as observations independent of DRAM admission.

load.input_state: Successful cold branch with bounded DRAM
load.observed_output: Clock/cache setup, app and U-Boot reads
load.independent_constraint: Check sector and byte spans, reservations and entry visibility before branch.

app.input_state: Loaded app, target, SRAM configuration and modeled CHIPID
app.observed_output: SFVD-normal transfer or unsupported write-back boundary
app.independent_constraint: Resolve relevant side effects or specify an alternative consumer interface.

uboot.input_state: Image and ABI state; bounded calls use raw AFI and mux
uboot.observed_output: RAM size and MMC registration plus selected environment
uboot.independent_constraint: Compatible U-Boot additionally needs its actual startup stack, relocation and reservations.

linux.input_state: Validated images, selected bootargs, completed kernel data setup
linux.observed_output: FDT, initrd and executed cleanup to first kernel instruction
linux.independent_constraint: Check ARM Linux protocol and target kernel/DT independently of the AFI ABI.

recovery.input_state: Early PMIC/GPIO or cold error branch
recovery.observed_output: ROM-copy/jump intent or earlier terminal; no downstream handoff
recovery.independent_constraint: Provide failure containment without assuming ROM re-entry or persistence is safe.

resume.input_state: PMIC flag and vector, retained memory expected
resume.observed_output: Mode-1 programming, resume jump or power-off boundary
resume.independent_constraint: Disable retention support until electrical and software prerequisites are resolved.

ini-printed-device.meaning: Printed as bootdev only; not the boot medium (both SD paths print 0x22)

gpio-enable.meaning: Little-endian word; nonzero enables the GPIO loopback test for nonzero boot code

pmic-bus.meaning: PMIC I2C bus index, copied to 0xb4070858[0]

pmic-byte-19.meaning: Copied to 0xb4070858[1]; consumer and significance open

pmic-byte-1a.meaning: Copied to 0xb407085c; consumer and significance open

pmic-adjust.meaning: Operand to the PMIC reg 0x14 calculation, copied to 0xb4070860

dram-select.meaning: Little-endian record-selection word; nonzero selects the secondary DRAM record on the cold path only

sfvd.meaning: Configuration write-back guard tested by app.bin

dram-mhz.meaning: Requested clock in MHz (u16 little-endian copied from the low half of a 4-byte INI slot). Cold mode rounds down to a 12 MHz multiple
dram-mhz.ini_uncopied_bytes: INI slot bytes above the copied u16 are ignored on input and zeroed by write-back

dram-mib.meaning: Capacity in MiB (u16 little-endian copied from the low half of a 4-byte INI slot). Cold timing starts from a forced 2048; the probe or failure path stores the final value
dram-mib.ini_uncopied_bytes: INI slot bytes above the copied u16 are ignored on input and zeroed by write-back

dram-bus.meaning: Input bus-width selector. Cold normalization (semantics.dram-bus): 0 fixed x32, 1 fixed x16, 2..255 x32 with automatic x16 fallback. The working byte then encodes the attempt width (0 = x32, 1 = x16); a persistent training failure stores min(input, 2)

dram-cs.meaning: Input chip-select selector. Cold normalization (semantics.dram-rank): 1 or 2 fixed; 0 and 3..255 automatic, trying two ranks then one. The working byte holds the attempt rank count; a persistent training failure stores the input when it is at most 2, else 0

dram-type.meaning: Low nibble 0 selects the DDR3-style branch, nonzero an LPDDR-class branch; high nibble 1 skips idle self-refresh programming

dram-rcc.meaning: Row code bits 7:6, column code bits 3:2, bank code bits 1:0 (0 selects the eight-bank capacity branch). The cold alias probe runs only when rcc & 0xcc == 0; the bank code is never probed

dram-tail.meaning: Copied and written back unchanged; significance open

rom-entry.behavior: Execution is modeled from a first sector at 0xb4060000. Physical PC, privilege, interrupt masks, CP15, ROM search and initial SRAM are unknown.
rom-entry.justification: A valid entry and usable memory are required before an independent frame is possible.
model_assumptions: SP 0xb409f000, CPSR 0x1d3, Unicorn CP15 and mapped SRAM are supplied.

boot-select.behavior: Reads gate word, tests bit 7 before bit 4, and writes code 2 or 0 at 0xb4064c00.
boot-select.justification: The branch is established. Gate labels and physical reset values do not define a portable medium detector.
model_assumptions: Gate read is an injected input, boot word is consumed by firmware instructions.

load-early.behavior: Calls 0xb4060400 with r9=4, r0=LBA 0x102b, r1=80, r2=0xb4065400. Success enters installed loader.
load-early.justification: Dependent on verified service semantics or equivalent loading.
model_assumptions: ROM service success returns zero and copies pinned sectors.

rom-read-failed.behavior: Synthetic service failure reaches block-0 idle.
rom-read-failed.justification: Report storage or ROM failure before DRAM.

globals.behavior: Clears 0x7c global bytes at 0xb4070800 and propagates settings.
globals.justification: Stock consumers expect initialized globals. An independent ABI can allocate its own state.

config-read.behavior: Reads LBA 0x1013, eight sectors to 0xb4062400, then decodes INI fields.
config-read.justification: DRAM and board choices depend on the configuration, while the disk format is vendor policy.

clock-basis.behavior: Firmware arithmetic assumes a 24 MHz basis: the delay target adds 24 ticks per requested microsecond and the UART divisor is udiv(24000000, 8*baud) minus one when nonzero. The physical oscillator is unmeasured.
clock-basis.justification: Clock source, divider and reset gates must be qualified before timing-sensitive operations.

timer.behavior: Gate bit 27, clear timer words, then set timer 0 control to 4.

else.why: Invalid INI is rejected before the ADFU check; the caller boundary bounds the same pre-recovery interval

delay.behavior: Compare signed count minus target, with target = start + 24 times requested microseconds.
delay.justification: Known delay availability matters for reset and PMIC sequences. A bounded alternate timebase can fulfill the role.
model_assumptions: Early timer increments by 2400 per read; DRAM calls are stubbed.

polling.wrap: correct for intervals shorter than 2^31 ticks

uart-reset.behavior: Select UART3/pad 0, gate it, pulse reset and program control/divider.
uart-reset.justification: Pre-DRAM output aids diagnosis. UART availability is not a demonstrated DRAM prerequisite.

uart-output.behavior: Wait while status bit 6 is set, write TX at +8, then wait for bit 10.
uart-output.justification: Controller setup and external signal routing are independent prerequisites.
model_assumptions: Loader printf is intercepted; app UART TX sees synthetic ready.

ini-reject.behavior: Version mismatch returns -1 to main recovery branch before DRAM.
ini-reject.justification: A loader needs a validated board record before applying it.

board-mux.behavior: Board index 1 clears 0xe39e0 and sets 0x619c0 in MFP_CTL2.
board-mux.justification: Later bounded MMC gets this word; necessity for physical mux/DRAM is unresolved.

pmic-clock.behavior: Clear MFP_CTL3 bit 30, branch on oscillator control bit 0 and wait 300 us if it was clear. Set pad and clock-out words.
pmic-clock.justification: Controller and PMIC physical prerequisites remain open.

i2c-setup.behavior: I2C1 gates bit 15, sets pull word bits 9 and 10, clears MFP field 0x50000, divider 0x10.
i2c-setup.justification: Select transport before reading board PMIC.

polling.scope: static only; bus transactions stubbed in unified path

pmic-id.behavior: Checks 0xff=0x00ca, probes slave 0x65, checks 0x32=0x1bc0, rejects unsupported identity.
pmic-id.justification: Configure only the selected and qualified board PMIC.
model_assumptions: PMIC file transactions are modeled at the I2C stub, physical identity unresolved.

pmic-51-configure.justification: Stock type-2 order is established; electrical effect remains unresolved.
model_assumptions: I2C stub values, width is PMIC payload rather than CPU bus width.

pmic-39-configure.justification: Stock type-2 order is established; electrical effect remains unresolved.
model_assumptions: I2C stub values, width is PMIC payload rather than CPU bus width.

pmic-11-configure.justification: Stock type-2 order is established; electrical effect remains unresolved.
model_assumptions: I2C stub values, width is PMIC payload rather than CPU bus width.

pmic-12-configure.justification: Stock type-2 order is established; electrical effect remains unresolved.
model_assumptions: I2C stub values, width is PMIC payload rather than CPU bus width.

pmic-14-configure.behavior: Write register 0x14 using 0x80ca | (adjust << 8), reference adjust maps 3 to 9.
pmic-14-configure.justification: Stock type-2 order is established; electrical effect remains unresolved.
model_assumptions: I2C stub values, width is PMIC payload rather than CPU bus width.

pmic-15-configure.justification: Stock type-2 order is established; electrical effect remains unresolved.
model_assumptions: I2C stub values, width is PMIC payload rather than CPU bus width.

pmic-16-configure.justification: Stock type-2 order is established; electrical effect remains unresolved.
model_assumptions: I2C stub values, width is PMIC payload rather than CPU bus width.

pmic-29-configure.justification: Stock type-2 order is established; electrical effect remains unresolved.
model_assumptions: I2C stub values, width is PMIC payload rather than CPU bus width.

pmic-00-configure.justification: Stock type-2 order is established; electrical effect remains unresolved.
model_assumptions: I2C stub values, width is PMIC payload rather than CPU bus width.

power-state.behavior: Read PMU_CTL3 and construct resume flags/vector from PMIC registers; restore or clear wake bits as indicated.
power-state.justification: Both modeled resume flag and vector must be present before using retained DRAM.

pmic-recovery-test.behavior: Read PMIC 0x35 first, check bit 1, and clear bits 0–1 before recovery. Read failure yields 0xffff in firmware.
pmic-recovery-test.justification: PMIC pending state has precedence over GPIO and may be an I2C error.

gpio-loopback.behavior: If enabled and code != 0, clear PULLCTL1 bit 17, sample 32 echoed bits and restore direction words. Exact echo enters recovery.
gpio-loopback.justification: Firmware recipes and omitted work have matching synthetic DRAM comparisons. Require separate validation of resulting pad state.
model_assumptions: C10 read semantics and pin mux interaction are hypothetical.

publish-pointers.behavior: Publishes six words at 0xb4064c60..0xb4064c77 before dispatch.
publish-pointers.justification: Stock stages may locate shared globals using the table.

cold-record.behavior: Retained state was not selected. When INI selector is nonzero, use the secondary working record.
cold-record.justification: Secondary cold configuration triggers detection for the shipped records.

resume-record.behavior: Both resume flag and vector were nonzero. Use the stored primary record in mode 1.
resume-record.justification: Retention depends on the previous memory configuration and vector ABI.

dram-gates-off.behavior: Read-modify-write disable DDR PLL enable and clear gate bits 1 and 3 at the start of each attempt.
dram-gates-off.justification: Observed at the start of each modeled programming pass; reset words are not established.

dram-reset.behavior: Clear and set reset bits 0 and 2 in DEVRST0.
dram-reset.justification: Each pass toggles the low reset bits; individual domain attribution is related-IP inference.

dram-pll-enable.behavior: DDRPLL receives F/12 | 0x300 for selected DDR clock, then gate bits 1 and 3 are enabled.
dram-pll-enable.justification: PLL arithmetic is verified; electrical readiness and bit 9 remain unknown.

phy-reset.justification: Firmware orders DLL toggle and status clear before programming timings.

ddr-mr1-program.justification: 20231014 changed data fields under identical code. Their board applicability remains unknown.

zq-control-program.justification: 20231014 changed data fields under identical code. Their board applicability remains unknown.

phy-timing.behavior: Program power control, MCFG, PUBL DCR, MR, PTR, DTPR, rank enables and I/O settings.
phy-timing.justification: Timing and mode-register words derive from clock, capacity class, type, width, chip selects and ODT.

zq-poll.behavior: Read ZQ0SR0 bit 31. Clear bit at all 101 reads yields internal 0x2a00fa11.
zq-poll.justification: Lack of ZQ completion prevents the firmware from issuing DRAM-init request.

phy-reset-poll.behavior: Wait for PGSR & 7 == 7 before PIR programming.
phy-reset-poll.justification: PIR issue follows required firmware status condition.

dram-init.behavior: PIR request 0x7f for cold DDR3, 0x5f for LPDDR-class or 0x3f on resume. Wait for exact PGSR 0xf.
dram-init.justification: Training does not start until the init poll succeeds; resume request effects remain unresolved.

phy-poll-terminal.behavior: Synthetic never-done response holds the firmware in a poll. Emulator terminates by instruction budget.
phy-poll-terminal.justification: Distinguish an execution cutoff from any firmware timeout.

resume-precharge.behavior: Issue eight PREA and eight REF to retained ranks prior to training.
resume-precharge.justification: Executed mode-1 preparation does not establish retained contents.

train.behavior: PIR=0x81 and exact PGSR decode. Error 0x3f samples lane status and may retry at reduced ranks or width.
train.justification: A trained status is distinct from usable capacity and physical validation.

train-passed.behavior: Branch reaches the controller path after PGSR training pass.
train-passed.justification: Distinguish responses from eventual controller-access state.

dfi-ready.behavior: Poll DFISTSTAT0 bit 0; read limit 101. Failure can participate in rank retry.
dfi-ready.justification: The controller timing sequence follows the readiness branch.

controller-timing.behavior: Program uPCTL timing words, DFI settings and command test. Reference tREFI is 3650 memory cycles.
controller-timing.justification: Requires selected board timings, DFI ready and correct bank/rank values.

controller-go.behavior: Request Config then GO through SCTL and verify reported state.
controller-go.justification: Capacity probe requires memory transactions after controller enters Access.

capacity-detect.behavior: Probe aliases under DMM column/row configurations; bank count comes from the record. Unsupported exponent may fail.
capacity-detect.justification: A verified fixed board geometry can replace adaptive probing if hardware identity and DMM semantics are known.

capacity-final.behavior: Program DCU_CFG with detected geometry in cold mode, stored geometry in resume.
capacity-final.justification: Actual mapping must agree with intended addressable memory.

memory-diagnostic.behavior: Write and read 24 power-of-two addresses and 252 strided words at 256 MiB. Print mismatch; caller ignores diagnostic return.
memory-diagnostic.justification: Independent admission needs a deliberate failure policy and sufficient address/data coverage.

config-writeback.behavior: Copy the working record to primary SRAM fields, including after returned cold error.
config-writeback.justification: Only retain the vendor record when its downstream consumers require it.

afi-produce.behavior: Clear and populate 16-byte record from boot code, UART settings and record capacity. Runs even on returned cold error.
afi-produce.justification: Retained U-Boot getters dereference the raw bytes. Independent Linux uses its own ABI.

main-recovery.behavior: Cold returned error reaches recovery after write-back and AFI.
main-recovery.justification: A plausible compatibility record cannot qualify the cold next-stage branch.

rom-reentry.behavior: Record copy of 0x2e00 bytes from 0xffff5200 to SRAM, CPU state update and final jump.
rom-reentry.justification: A bounded terminal need not reuse vendor recovery. The actual copied payload and entry remain unknown.
model_assumptions: ROM copy is logged, no ROM bytes are available.

resume-transfer.behavior: A successful retention scenario jumps to its saved vector.
resume-transfer.justification: The actual consumer has a separate CPU and memory contract.

resume-power-off.behavior: On failure rearm PMIC alarm and reach power-off loop.
resume-power-off.justification: Retained-memory failure cannot fall into cold executable load unless another policy is validated.

cold-continue.behavior: Return zero from cold dispatcher reaches actual loading path even when the stock diagnostic failed.
cold-continue.justification: Compatibility transfer requires this executed continuation and validated current memory.

post-dram-clock.behavior: Main sets SCTLR.I and enters storage-related clock setup.
post-dram-clock.justification: Qualify executable memory visibility and clock state; observed settings are board-specific.

load-app-uboot.behavior: Read app.bin at 0x1000, stage U-Boot header, read U-Boot sectors from LBA 0x1800 with image at 0x05000000.
load-app-uboot.justification: Verify bounded destination, entire on-disk span, entry and integrity before executing.

reject-placement.behavior: A detected 64 MiB cannot contain the vendor U-Boot destination at 80 MiB.
reject-placement.justification: Every loader should bound the entire interval, including sector rounding, against validated RAM and reserved spans.

app-sfvd.behavior: Preserve AFI, check CHIPID and the SFVD word, then branch to saved entry on the normal path.
app-sfvd.justification: A replacement must fulfill relevant U-Boot preconditions and define persistence policy.
model_assumptions: CHIPID status/data and chip revision responses are synthetic.

app-write-intent.behavior: If SFVD absent, branch to write-back. Bounded run records intent without performing I/O.
app-write-intent.justification: Only necessary for deployments retaining conditional persistent vendor INI updates.

uboot-entry.behavior: app.bin lands at the loaded entry address in masked SVC mode with AFI preserved.
uboot-entry.justification: Needed only for this consumer and pinned startup contract.

uboot-relocate.behavior: Pinned Koriki binary has a local stack literal, r9 global data and relocation copy/fixups. Runtime layout unresolved.
uboot-relocate.justification: Model helper stack and global-data addresses do not define compatible startup.

afi-consume.behavior: Reads the exact AFI bytes. Writes acceptable size to gd+0x34, otherwise uses 496 MiB fallback.
afi-consume.justification: Bounded consumer proves byte dependence, while runtime allocation remains unknown.

mmc-register.behavior: SD0 still registers device 0 if its card is absent. SD2 registers device 1 for the reconstructed SD2 role.
mmc-register.justification: Distinguish controller identity, registration order and card presence.

boot-device.behavior: Boot command uses AFI device 0x20 for mmcboot, 0x22 for emmcboot.
boot-device.justification: Independent storage should bind stable controller/card and partition identity.

fat-load.behavior: Bounded environment selects backing controller and FAT partition 1, then requests kernel, ramdisk and DTB.
fat-load.justification: Declare supported storage policy and validate the full extents. Other environment commands and redundant arbitration remain gaps.

memory-plan.behavior: Build memory bank, check resident regions, input reservations and decompression envelope.
memory-plan.justification: Prevent wrap and overlap with all live images/metadata and actual relocation zones.

device-tree.behavior: Fix up DT memory and chosen data using actual loaded image, AFI-derived RAM, command line and initrd bounds.
device-tree.justification: FDT describes validated usable memory, devices and reservations to the target kernel.

linux-entry.behavior: Execute cleanup and branch to kernel entry with ARM SVC, IRQ/FIQ masked and MMU/D-cache off.
linux-entry.justification: ARM Linux ABI and target image both constrain register/CPU state; kernel has yet to run.

rom-entry--boot-select.why: The scenario supplies the initial gate word and first instructions.

boot-select--load-early.why: The selected block-0 branch requests the early-loader read.
boot-select--load-early.occurrence_justification: boot-select also covers the early loader reading the boot-code word at 0xb4065414 after it is installed; only the block-0 producer occurrence precedes the ROM load

load-early--globals.why: Main runs from the installed span.

load-early--config-read.why: The installed main code makes the INI request.

globals--config-read.why: Main clears its stock globals before the read.

config-read--cold-record.why: The cold selector comes from the reloaded INI.

config-read--resume-record.why: Mode 1 uses the original primary configuration.

clock-basis--timer.why: The clock source must be sufficient for the elapsed-time calculation.

timer--delay.why: Delay polls timer 0 count after enabling the timer.

timer--uart-reset.why: The startup sequence calls timer before UART reset and uses its count for the reset pulse.

delay--uart-reset.why: UART reset pulse asks for 1 microsecond.

uart-reset--uart-output.why: Transmit requires a configured controller and acceptable TX status.

uart-reset--board-mux.why: UART is initialized early; its controller setup does not write the selected mux.

uart-output--cold-record.why: Diagnostic setup precedes DRAM without a demonstrated physical necessity.

delay--pmic-clock.why: Firmware waits for the oscillator control transition when needed.

board-mux--pmic-clock.why: The configuration-dependent pin setup precedes clock-out selection.

pmic-clock--i2c-setup.why: Clock-out and I2C setup precede PMIC identification; actual electrical prerequisite is open.

i2c-setup--pmic-id.why: Bus selection is made before reading the identity registers.

pmic-id--pmic-51-configure.why: Register programming follows successful type-2 detection.

pmic-id--pmic-39-configure.why: Register programming follows successful type-2 detection.

pmic-id--pmic-11-configure.why: Register programming follows successful type-2 detection.

pmic-id--pmic-12-configure.why: Register programming follows successful type-2 detection.

pmic-id--pmic-14-configure.why: Register programming follows successful type-2 detection.

pmic-id--pmic-15-configure.why: Register programming follows successful type-2 detection.

pmic-id--pmic-16-configure.why: Register programming follows successful type-2 detection.

pmic-id--pmic-29-configure.why: Register programming follows successful type-2 detection.

pmic-id--pmic-00-configure.why: Register programming follows successful type-2 detection.

pmic-51-configure--pmic-39-configure.why: Cold reference PMIC order. Electrical dependency is unresolved.

pmic-39-configure--pmic-11-configure.why: Cold reference PMIC order. Electrical dependency is unresolved.

pmic-11-configure--pmic-12-configure.why: Cold reference PMIC order. Electrical dependency is unresolved.

pmic-12-configure--pmic-14-configure.why: Cold reference PMIC order. Electrical dependency is unresolved.

pmic-14-configure--pmic-15-configure.why: Cold reference PMIC order. Electrical dependency is unresolved.

pmic-15-configure--pmic-16-configure.why: Cold reference PMIC order. Electrical dependency is unresolved.

pmic-16-configure--pmic-29-configure.why: Cold reference PMIC order. Electrical dependency is unresolved.

pmic-29-configure--power-state.why: Cold PMIC configuration precedes wake-state sampling.

power-state--pmic-00-configure.why: Resume determination governs cold status updates.

pmic-id--power-state.why: Power-state reading follows successful PMIC selection.

power-state--pmic-recovery-test.why: Main calls recovery policy after pmu_init completion.

pmic-recovery-test--gpio-loopback.why: A PMIC recovery branch prevents GPIO access.

boot-select--gpio-loopback.why: Boot code zero suppresses the GPIO branch.

delay--gpio-loopback.why: Each sampled bit follows a requested 1000 us wait.

gpio-loopback--cold-record.why: Normal nonzero code returns from GPIO before DRAM; physical dependency remains open.

gpio-loopback--dram-gates-off.why: Possible pad electrical effects remain open despite matching modeled DRAM order.

pmic-recovery-test--rom-reentry.why: Early pending status or exact GPIO echo can take ROM re-entry.

pmic-recovery-test--publish-pointers.why: A recovery return bypasses pointer publication.

publish-pointers--cold-record.why: Publication precedes record dispatch in verified instructions.

power-state--resume-record.why: Saved flag and vector select mode 1.

power-state--dram-gates-off.why: PMIC settings precede DRAM; rail effects and settling requirements are unresolved.

resume-record--dram-gates-off.why: Mode-1 entry supplies the primary record.

delay--dram-reset.why: Firmware delays during the PLL/gate/reset and PHY sequence.

dram-gates-off--dram-reset.why: Order within each stock programming attempt; analog dependency is unverified.

dram-reset--dram-pll-enable.why: The release operation precedes PLL programming and gate enable in each pass.

dram-pll-enable--phy-reset.why: Preserve the observed clock and reset order pending documented accessibility and settling.

phy-reset--phy-timing.why: The stock DLL and status clear precede programming the controller and PHY.

phy-timing--zq-poll.why: Timing and I/O words precede ZQ completion checks.

zq-poll--phy-reset-poll.why: ZQ timeout returns before PHY reset status poll.

phy-reset-poll--dram-init.why: The initial PGSR status gates PIR DRAM-init request.

dram-init--resume-precharge.why: Mode 1 issues retained-memory commands before training.

dram-init--train.why: Training cannot start until the initialization poll succeeds.

resume-precharge--train.why: The initial PREA/REF bursts precede training in mode 1.

train--train-passed.why: Only the pass response permits the DFI path.

train-passed--dfi-ready.why: Successful training reaches the DFI poll.

dfi-ready--controller-timing.why: The DFI result gates timing and controller programming.

controller-timing--controller-go.why: The controller timing and ready checks precede GO.

controller-go--capacity-detect.why: The address probe executes after GO on the shipped cold configuration.

capacity-detect--capacity-final.why: The decode results determine the final DMM config.

resume-record--capacity-final.why: Resume uses the stored geometry without the cold probe.

capacity-final--memory-diagnostic.why: The measured capacity is the diagnostic argument.

memory-diagnostic--config-writeback.why: The caller ignores the diagnostic result and continues to write-back.

capacity-final--config-writeback.why: The updated geometry is written to primary SRAM. Returned failures instead write fallback fields.

config-writeback--afi-produce.why: Same working record supplies write-back and the AFI size helper.

boot-select--afi-produce.why: Boot word determines AFI device byte.

afi-produce--main-recovery.why: Cold failure can publish AFI but cannot execute load continuation.

afi-produce--cold-continue.why: Main tests the caller return, independently of whether AFI is present.

cold-continue--post-dram-clock.why: Execution reaches clock/cache setup through the real cold continuation.

load-app-uboot--app-sfvd.why: Code and the header-selected entry argument are live in DRAM.

app-sfvd--uboot-entry.why: SFVD-present app branches to the saved entry.

app-sfvd--app-write-intent.why: Alternate marker condition reaches unsupported write-back.

uboot-entry--uboot-relocate.why: Static startup path exists, while runtime reservation and global-data objects remain unknown.

afi-produce--afi-consume.why: Exact raw AFI bytes are used by U-Boot getters without reconstruction.

uboot-entry--afi-consume.why: The bounded invocation inherits payload and AFI while bypassing startup.

board-mux--mmc-register.why: Bounded MMC seeds its initial mux word from the loader.

afi-consume--mmc-register.why: AFI identifies the expected controller role.

mmc-register--boot-device.why: Assigned device indices and card outcomes supply the script storage context.

afi-consume--boot-device.why: The actual check_boot_flag reads AFI to select its command.

boot-device--fat-load.why: The bounded script selects the actual image backing the expected controller and partition.

fat-load--memory-plan.why: Each loaded interval and the decompressor envelope must fit validated DRAM.

afi-consume--device-tree.why: Board data receives the actual gd RAM size before executing DT fixups.

memory-plan--device-tree.why: LMB input and image intervals constrain FDT fixups and in-place growth.

fat-load--device-tree.why: Fixups operate on loaded DT and ramdisk ranges.

device-tree--linux-entry.why: The fixup result feeds the executed Linux transfer r2.

capacity-final--resume-transfer.why: Successful mode-1 setup precedes the retained-vector jump.

cold-linux.rule: Cold dispatch and validated downstream state are required.

rom-failure.rule: Synthetic service failure stops before loading main.

bad-ini.rule: INI check rejects before programming DRAM.

early-recovery.rule: Pending PMIC or GPIO echo terminates before DRAM.

cold-failed.rule: AFI and error dispatch occur together.

phy-stall.rule: Trace budget establishes terminal classification only.

retained-vector.rule: Retained vector is separate from cold dispatch.

retained-failed.rule: Failure ends at PMIC power-off boundary.

image-range.rule: Valid DRAM initialization can still produce an invalid image destination.

app-unsupported.rule: SFVD absent stops at write intent.

rom-entry-state.consequence: Entry PC, instruction set, privilege, stack and CP15 must permit controlled execution.
rom-entry-state.offline: Audit first-stage instructions for inherited assumptions. ROM image is absent.
rom-entry-state.future_observation: Earliest possible stock entry state for selected medium.
rom-entry-state.discriminates: Determines initial execution mode and which state may safely be established.

rom-medium-state.consequence: Medium changes may alter gates, pad state or ROM service behavior.
rom-medium-state.offline: Compare verified block-0 branches and accurately scoped vendor labels.
rom-medium-state.future_observation: Comparable entry snapshots by supported medium.
rom-medium-state.discriminates: Separates stock bit test from a stable hardware medium indication.

sram-ownership.consequence: Unknown extent, aliasing, ROM-resident code and stack boundaries constrain any independent image.
sram-ownership.offline: Inventory live spans and stage accesses.
sram-ownership.future_observation: Evidence of ROM-populated bytes and available non-overlapping SRAM.
sram-ownership.discriminates: Bounds safe code, data and stack placement.

rom-service.consequence: Loading service and error semantics may constrain the first replaceable stage.
rom-service.offline: Verify register conventions at caller sites and separate observed call sites from model behavior.
rom-service.future_observation: Verified Boot ROM loading ABI and inherited service availability on this board.
rom-service.discriminates: Resolves service selector, storage results and memory clobbers.

clock-reset.consequence: PLL settling, oscillator source, gate/reset semantics and initial values control all timings.
clock-reset.offline: Reconcile matching-revision clock descriptions and numeric RMW anchors.
clock-reset.future_observation: Stock clock/reset snapshots and correlated timing evidence.
clock-reset.discriminates: Establishes clock rate and reset baseline versus inherited guesses.

pmic-identity.consequence: The selected regulator program must target the actual board PMIC.
pmic-identity.offline: Compare pinned board DT and exact revision identity documentation.
pmic-identity.future_observation: Independent PMIC part identification for board revision.
pmic-identity.discriminates: Constrains applicable capability and register map.

pmic-rails.consequence: Unknown rail and wake effects prevent qualifying cold setup.
pmic-rails.offline: Find and match authoritative register and PMU source revisions.
pmic-rails.future_observation: Stock rail state and regulator sequencing evidence.
pmic-rails.discriminates: Determines enabling, settling and safety prerequisites.

dram-device.consequence: Part identity, revision and geometry determine valid timings and decode.
dram-device.offline: Compare part data when identified and rule out alternative DMM decode assumptions.
dram-device.future_observation: Board and DRAM device identification for tested release.
dram-device.discriminates: Separates same-capacity geometries and fixes device electrical specifications.

phy-revision.consequence: Matching offsets do not establish identical PHY fields or controller semantics.
phy-revision.future_observation: Target controller and PHY revision identification.
phy-revision.discriminates: Qualifies programming semantics across related IP layouts.

training-timing.consequence: Synthetic status cannot establish real training, ZQ or electrical timing.
training-timing.offline: Reconcile request, poll and return paths with matched hardware documentation.
training-timing.future_observation: Stock early DDR console and status, timing and lane observations.
training-timing.discriminates: Distinguishes training pattern, readiness, rank retry and clock behavior.

board-variants.consequence: Different ODT and GPIO strap scopes need verified board applicability.
board-variants.offline: Compare shipped INI/DT combinations and vendor board data.
board-variants.future_observation: Board identities paired with stock clocks, memory and strap.
board-variants.discriminates: Determines which profiles can share a configuration.

gpio-semantics.consequence: GPIO readback versus mux priority determines what state survives after removing the stock check.
gpio-semantics.offline: Compare pinned pinctrl and matched GPIO documentation.
gpio-semantics.future_observation: Observation of stock mux and input/latch state across the decision.
gpio-semantics.discriminates: Distinguishes GPIO samples from latched bits and qualifies pad replacement.

uart-routing.consequence: Early console can be unavailable with controller configured.
uart-routing.offline: Identify likely pinctrl assignments and affected board routes.
uart-routing.discriminates: Determines whether diagnostics can be observed externally.

app-alternates.consequence: Alternate paths can update SRAM-backed settings or pad state.
app-alternates.offline: Trace selected consumers and conditions in the app call graph.
app-alternates.future_observation: Stock state comparisons before/after alternate app path.
app-alternates.discriminates: Distinguishes required setup, service behavior and persistence side effects.

uboot-reservations.consequence: Startup stack, computed reservation and relocated ranges can overlap otherwise valid image buffers.
uboot-reservations.offline: Trace board_f and allocator path and static startup landmarks.
uboot-reservations.future_observation: A trustworthy stock U-Boot startup/relocation memory map.
uboot-reservations.discriminates: Bounds memory lifetime through relocation and board setup.

environment-redundancy.consequence: Valid persistent copies may select a different boot policy.
environment-redundancy.offline: Reconstruct valid CRC and flag arbitration with controlled copies in files.
environment-redundancy.future_observation: Stock environment copy state when both are valid.
environment-redundancy.discriminates: Separates defaults in pinned runs from live redundant policy.

resume-reset.consequence: Electrical effect of PIR 0x3f may invalidate retention.
resume-reset.offline: Identify exact PHY revision and matching reset semantics.
resume-reset.future_observation: Stock retained-memory path and RESET# behavior.
resume-reset.discriminates: Determines whether mode 1 can be enabled without destructive reset.

platform-kernel.consequence: A modern kernel needs applicable device tree, timer/GIC, SMP and storage support.
platform-kernel.offline: Verify the exact target kernel entry/board support and compare pinned legacy DT.
platform-kernel.future_observation: Early Linux output and immutable board behavior for the chosen modern kernel.
platform-kernel.discriminates: Separates a valid ARM entry from functioning platform support.

a.name: ROM-compatible SRAM execution
a.maturity: Stock SRAM instructions anchored. Physical ROM entry unknown.
prerequisites: Verified supported medium, entry rules and writable/executable SRAM
Private aligned stack and explicit CPU/exception-state policy
validation: Check image bounds, entry requirements and SRAM coexistence
Classify early failure without needing DRAM or UART
a.promotion: Demonstrate controlled SRAM execution with known entry and documented placement.

b.name: Independent DRAM initialization
b.maturity: Register operations and timing model established for offline design. Physical dependencies open.
prerequisites: Verified board clocks, resets, PMIC rails and memory device
Reviewed controller, DFI, PHY programming and failure policy
validation: Reject unsupported geometry and failed or unverified memory before loading
b.promotion: Establish validated usable memory and typed init failure outcomes.

c.name: Independent early loader with compatible U-Boot
c.maturity: AFI ABI and bounded consumers verified. Startup relocation and app alternates remain open.
prerequisites: Reproduce exact compatible AFI layout and interface
Qualify U-Boot startup state, image placement and app-owned preconditions
validation: Bound load, startup stack and relocation spans
Verify medium, board configuration and exact compatible consumer entry
c.promotion: Account for retained consumer requirements or choose an independently specified second-stage interface.

d.name: Independent Linux bootstrap
d.maturity: Legacy handoff reproduced to entry; modern platform support requires separate validation.
prerequisites: Verified image, FDT, initrd and reserved intervals
Qualified CPU/interrupt/cache state and target kernel board support
validation: Check actual Linux ABI, decompression and platform assumptions
Verify stable boot-medium selection independent of device enumeration
d.promotion: A validated entry can progress to platform bring-up for a specific tree and kernel.

retry_transitions.when: Training PIR returns PGSR 0x3f (internal 0x1017fa11) and semantics.dram-retry leaves a rank or width candidate
retry_transitions.bound: At most four attempts (input bus >= 2 with automatic ranks); two with the shipped x16 secondary record

ranges.owner: Block 0 instructions and literals; app.bin later saves its target at 0xb4060018
Zero-filled on disk; ROM service entry 0xb4060400 and alternate reader 0xb40612b0 inferred ROM-populated
Static app.bin alternate writer: 20 sectors from 0xb4062400 to LBA 0x1013 (not executed)
INI reloaded by main (selector 4, LBA 0x1013); SFVD at +0x400
Early loader installed by the block-0 ROM call (selector 4, LBA 0x102b)
I2C bus cache inside the installed loader image
Globals cleared by main; working DRAM records at 0xb4070820 and 0xb407084c
Requested ROM copy destination in the ADFU re-entry path
Requested ROM copy source; contents absent
SP assigned at ROM re-entry; down-growing; depth unknown
Emulator SP; the ROM-provided physical SP is unknown

overlaps.why: ADFU re-entry abandons the cold path and overwrites block 0
Recovery runs instead of AFI consumers
Recovery no longer calls the earlier service through these addresses
Copy through 0xb4062e00 overwrites the first 0xa00 INI bytes
The static write-back source is not used after recovery
The alternate writer persists the reloaded INI and twelve further sectors of unresolved provenance
Cache word lives in the installed image

generation.note: Produced after every returned cold DRAM call, including failures (2048 MiB fallback). Not produced by resume, early recovery, invalid INI, ROM failure or an unbounded poll.

admission.note: A stock consumer runs only after main continuation with a zero DRAM return. Valid AFI bytes alone do not establish DRAM initialization.

afi.linux_note: Linux receives memory through the device tree. AFI is a stock U-Boot input only.

arm-linux-dt.kernel_entry: from validated image and target protocol

reference_fdt_reservation.note: The ordered Linux-entry traces show an FDT reservation made before the final fixups grow the blob. An independent loader should reserve the final blob size. The stock runtime allocation map remains open.

dram-bus.scope: Cold mode only (resume flag at 0xb4070804 zero), before the DDR3/LPDDR type branch at 0xb40674e4. Resume uses the stored working byte without normalization or retry.

names.bus_width_bits: 32 when the working byte is 0, else 16
names.capacity_width_operand: 1 for x16, 2 for x32; also the density divisor

dram-rank.scope: Cold mode only. Resume uses the stored chip-select byte; zero there divides by zero in the density calculation.

dram-retry.eligibility: Only PGSR 0x3f after the training PIR (0xb40687a8) yields 0x1017fa11 and reaches the retry test
dram-retry.reentry: Every retry re-enters at 0xb40674dc and repeats clock, reset, PHY and controller programming

dram-capacity.applies: After a trained cold attempt and controller GO. Resume stores no new capacity.
dram-capacity.arithmetic: Unsigned 32-bit; exponent = terms + 23 with chip_select_count 1 or 2. Accepted exponent 25..31 (32..2048 MiB eight-bank). Eight-bank value (0x10000 << (e - 20)) >> 16; other banks ((3 << (e - 20)) << 14) >> 16. Stored as a u16 in working bytes +2/+3.
limitations: Firmware arithmetic only; not a physical DRAM geometry formula
Nonzero bank codes below 256 MiB make the final DCU_CFG term ((cap >> 8) - 1) wrap (observed 0xffffff2c)
Probe aliasing and unsupported geometries can under- or over-report capacity
